summary: Sporting News marks the end of Showtime Championship Boxing, whose final broadcast is December 16, 2023, with David Morrell defending against Sena Agbeko in Minneapolis. The series began in 1986 and featured many boxing legends. The article revisits its five greatest fights: Hagler-Mugabi, Duran-Barkley, Tyson-Holyfield 1, Corrales-Castillo 1 and Vazquez-Marquez 3.
one_line: Sporting News looks back at the five greatest fights in Showtime Boxing history as the series ends its run in December 2023.
key_facts: Showtime Championship Boxing's final broadcast is December 16, 2023, headlined by David Morrell defending his WBA "regular" super middleweight title against Sena Agbeko at the Armory in Minneapolis.
Showtime Boxing began in 1986; its maiden broadcast was Marvelous Marvin Hagler vs. John Mugabi on March 10, 1986 at Caesars Palace, Las Vegas.
Hagler knocked out John Mugabi in round 11; Mugabi had entered with a perfect record of 26 fights, 26 wins, 26 knockouts.

Roberto Duran beat Iran Barkley by split decision (12 rounds) on February 24, 1989 in Atlantic City to win the WBC middleweight title, aged 37, becoming the first Hispanic fighter to win four world titles in as many weight classes.
Mike Tyson vs. Evander Holyfield 1 took place November 9, 1996 at the MGM Grand, Las Vegas; Holyfield won by TKO in round 11 after knocking Tyson down in round six.
Tyson was jailed for rape in 1992 and released in March 1995, then regained the WBC title by stopping Frank Bruno in three rounds and the WBA title by beating Bruce Seldon in one.

Diego Corrales stopped Jose Luis Castillo in round 10 on May 7, 2005 at Mandalay Bay Events Centre, Las Vegas, after being knocked down twice in the 10th and losing a point for spitting out his mouthpiece.
Israel Vazquez beat Rafael Marquez by split decision on March 1, 2008 at Home Depot Centre, Carson, California, to retain the WBC and Ring Magazine super bantamweight titles.
Vazquez-Marquez 3 won Fight of the Year for 2008; the first fight (won by Marquez) was beaten for 2007 Fight of the Year by the rematch (won by Vazquez).
Showtime Sports executive Stephen Espinoza said the decision was not a reflection of the work done, citing a rapidly evolving media marketplace.
HBO departed from boxing in 2018, which the article compares to Showtime's exit.
